Locked because “Require NFC to disable Switchly” is active.

Scan your paired NFC tag to disable Switchly and unlock protected controls. If QR unlock is enabled, you can use your QR fallback instead. After unlocking, schedules and protected settings are editable again.

Only accept NFC toggles from tags you have paired.\nPair tags in Settings → NFC tags, then use “Manage paired tags” to rename or remove them. If at least one UID is paired, only paired tags can toggle/unlock Switchly.

Pairing is currently disabled.\nWhat it does: if you pair at least one NFC tag, only paired tags can toggle/unlock Switchly (prevents random tags).\nHow to enable: Settings → Blocking & control toggles → Enable paired NFC tags.
Off by default. When enabled, writing a Switchly NFC tag will also store that tag UID as a paired tag. Use this only if you intentionally want writing and pairing to happen together.

Focus on calendar routines. NFC and QR actions are ignored while this mode is active.
Focus on physical friction. NFC actions are accepted for automation, including written tags and paired tags.
Focus on QR workflows. NFC and schedules are ignored while this mode is active.
Flexible mode with per-channel controls. Use the channel controls below to choose which control methods and active-access exceptions are allowed.

Lets NFC actions control Switchly, including written tags and paired tags. In Mixed mode, other allowed channels continue to work too.
Lets the home button and Quick Settings tile turn Switchly on and off in any control mode. When this is enabled, enable-only is hidden.
Lets you open app picker while Switchly is active.
Lets you manage or switch profiles while Switchly is active. Otherwise this stays locked for safety.
Lets you add, edit, delete, and toggle schedules while Switchly is active.
Lets you write and pair new NFC tags while Switchly is active.
When enabled, schedule automations are allowed to change Switchly state while Mixed mode is active.
When enabled, NFC actions are accepted while Mixed mode is active, including written tags and paired tags. Other allowed channels continue to work too.
When enabled, QR control is allowed in Mixed mode.
When enabled, the home button and Quick Settings tile can fully control Switchly, including disabling it. Turn this off if buttons should only start focus mode.
Safety default is locked while Switchly is enabled. Enable this only if you intentionally want app list edits while protection is active, regardless of the selected control mode.
Safety default is locked while Switchly is enabled. Enable this only if you intentionally want profile management or switching while protection is active.
Safety default is locked while Switchly is enabled. Enable this only if you intentionally want writing or pairing new NFC tags while protection is active, regardless of the selected control mode.
Disable Switchly to edit control methods and access rules.
When enabled, saved barcode actions are accepted in Mixed mode.
Lock Switchly screens while protection is active.
When enabled, Switchly settings and control screens are blocked while protection is active. Disable Switchly first (via an allowed channel) to change settings again.
Makes App Info, installers, and Play Store uninstall paths harder to use while Switchly is active.

Switchly is making uninstall-related screens harder to access while protection is active. This is friction, not true uninstall blocking. Disable Switchly first via your allowed method if you want to continue.
Lets the home button and Quick Settings tile turn Switchly on even when button disabling is not allowed. Disabling still requires NFC, QR, barcode, or another allowed control method.
When enabled, the home button and Quick Settings tile can turn Switchly on in any control mode. Turning it off still requires the currently allowed control methods.
Control mode is locked while Switchly is on. Disable Switchly first, then choose a mode.

Website editing is locked while Switchly is active. Disable Switchly first.
App limit editing is locked while Switchly is active. Disable Switchly first.
Switchly settings are locked while protection is active. Disable Switchly first to edit settings.
Lets you use the Switchly tile from Android Quick Settings. After enabling it here, add the tile from Android’s Quick Settings edit screen.
Filters notifications from apps that are currently blocked by your active profile. Requires notification listener access.
After a reboot, Switchly tries to start itself again so your protection profile comes back automatically.
Allows one temporary unlock per day (15 minutes). During this window, Switchly is disabled so you can quickly access blocked apps.
